headline: Keep the frontier of every reachable index
statement: Given nonnegative nums, you start at index zero. nums[i] is the maximum forward jump length from i; you may choose any shorter length. Return whether you can reach the final index.
prerequisites: Basic Python lists, loops, and functions
intuition: Track the farthest position you can reach. When you visit a reachable position, its jump length may extend that distance. You do not need to remember the route. If you reach a position beyond the farthest reachable point, no earlier jump can cross that gap.
approach: If index i exceeds farthest, return false.
Return true when farthest reaches the final index.
correctness: Before processing i, every index through farthest is reachable using processed positions. A reachable i extends that prefix by its jump interval. If i lies outside the prefix, no earlier position can reach it or any later position, so failure is final. Reaching the last index proves success.
bruteForce: Explore every jump from each reachable position, taking O(n^2) in a worst-case DP formulation; naive recursive paths may be exponential.

complexity.explanation: Each index is inspected at most once and only one frontier is retained.

pitfalls: nums[i] is a maximum, not a mandatory jump length.
A zero is harmless if an earlier jump can cross it.
A single-element input succeeds without moving.
